subject.title: [Bug]: Config validator rejects mediaLocalRoots despite type definitions supporting it (Telegram outbound)

question: Should OpenClaw expose persistent host-local media roots through Telegram-specific config, agent defaults, or a shared filesystem-root policy?
rationale: The implementation choice changes a security-sensitive config surface and may overlap with broader `tools.fs.roots` work, so automation should not pick the permanent contract.

options.title: Use shared root policy
options.body: Adopt a single `tools.fs.roots`-style contract for host filesystem and outbound media roots, then wire Telegram through that resolved policy.

options.title: Add Telegram-scoped roots
options.body: Add a narrow `channels.telegram.mediaLocalRoots` config surface with explicit docs and tests, accepting the extra channel-specific policy surface.

options.title: Document no new key
options.body: Keep the current schema, clarify supported staging and filesystem-policy behavior, and close the config-key request as not planned.

recommendation.title: Use shared root policy
recommendation.body: Adopt a single `tools.fs.roots`-style contract for host filesystem and outbound media roots, then wire Telegram through that resolved policy.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent outbound media/root-policy commits make this the closest current ownership trail.
